subject: Chemistry
q: The graph compares vapour pressure with temperature for liquids X, Y and Z. Consider: (A) X has stronger intermolecular interactions than Y; (B) X has weaker intermolecular interactions than Y; (C) Z has weaker intermolecular interactions than Y. Which inference is correct?
imgAlt: Vapour-pressure curves ordered X, Y and Z from left to right; X reaches any fixed vapour pressure at the lowest temperature and Z at the highest.
hint: At a fixed vapour pressure, the liquid requiring the lower temperature has weaker intermolecular attraction.
solution: For a given vapour pressure, X requires the lowest temperature, followed by Y and then Z. Equivalently, at a common temperature X is the most volatile. Thus intermolecular-force strength increases X < Y < Z. Only statement (B), that X has weaker intermolecular interactions than Y, is correct.
